maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-pick tweak for quant paths on sm89 we're seeing a perf dip for short seqs in a few workloads. Not a huge regression but reproducible. Can we triage?

sahil: saw that in dashboards. looks like the pick now prefers the fp8-mixed matmul for batch sizes < 4, which hurts int4 hotpath.

jin: can you paste the perf-bot run? also which model/seq are we talking about?

maya: quick snapshot from perf-bot run on staging cluster:

perf-bot: ```
benchmark: gpt-medium-q (hybrid int4+fp8)
arch: sm89
config: new-selector (mem_stride_bias=0.15, seqlen_breakpoints=[64,256])
seq=16 batch=1: 24.8 tok/s 
seq=32 batch=1: 26.1 tok/s
seq=128 batch=2: 10.9 tok/s

baseline (old-selector):
seq=16 batch=1: 28.7 tok/s
seq=32 batch=1: 29.4 tok/s
seq=128 batch=2: 9.8 tok/s
```

maya: so short seq regress, long seq improved. pattern suggests selector favors an fp8 matmul kernel for small matrices because of lower FLOP-estimate after the new workspace estimator.

lucas: hmm that estimator change was supposed to reduce workspace for long seqs. seems like it overcorrected for small N dims.

sahil: hypothesis: our kernel score = latency_est + mem_stride_bias * stride_penalty + q_savings. mem_stride_bias 0.15 is too high for sm89 with L2 prefetch patterns. small K dims get penalized incorrectly.

jin: agree. quick test patch idea: add an arch override map for mem_stride_bias per SM (e.g., sm89->0.06, sm92->0.12) and add a seqlen floor so for seq<=48 prefer int4-native kernel if token_density high.

maya: can we try a canary with mem_stride_bias=0.06 for sm89 on the staging GPU pool? also add a conservative seqlen_breakpoints for routing: [48,256].

lucas: I'll push a flag-only rollout. command: `./runtime/deploy --canary selector:mem_stride_bias=0.06 --filter nodepool=staging-sm89`

perf-bot: triggering microbenchmarks (will post results) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sahil: also worth adding a small penalty for kernel-change cost when KV cache active — switching matmul variants in the middle of generation can touch tuning caches and cause +5-10% jitter.

maya: good point. maybe a hysteresis on kernel picks when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.5 (e.g., require 1.15x improvement to switch).

jin: sketch of config knobs to add to selector: `arch_overrides:{sm89:{mem_stride_bias:0.06}}, seqlen_floor_switch:48, kv_hysteresis:1.15`

sahil: quick perf-bot followup (after canary):

perf-bot: ```
canary results (sm89 staging): mem_stride_bias=0.06, seqlen_breakpoints=[48,256]
seq=16 batch=1: 28.1 tok/s (+13%)
seq=32 batch=1: 29.0 tok/s (+11%)
seq=128 batch=2: 10.7 tok/s (-2%)
notes: long-seq still slightly better than baseline.
```

lucas: great, that aligns with hypothesis. will open a small PR to add arch_overrides and kv_hysteresis.

maya: thanks. let's keep the default conservative for hosted customers until we have per-arch vetted profiles. I'll add a rollout checklist: perf regressions <3% for seq<=64, <5% for seq<=128, and no correctness drift.

jin: +1. also add an integration test that runs on synthetic short-seq traffic to ensure no regressions land in main.

sahil: one more note — we should log the selector decision reasons into trace spans (kernel_id, score_breakdown) so SRE can debug future oddities without re-running benchmarks. small change but high signal.

maya: agree. put that on the PR too.

lucas: PR drafted: #3721 — adds arch_overrides, kv_hysteresis, and trace tags. tagging @perf-team for review.

maya: awesome. if all green we'll merge and start a staged rollout. :rocket:

perf-bot: merged perf run pending, will post final numbers in ~30m.
